response.sql:
WITH rep_counts AS (
  SELECT e.EmployeeId, e.City, COUNT(c.CustomerId) as customer_count
  FROM Customer c
  INNER JOIN Employee e ON c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId
  GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.City
),
city_averages AS (
  SELECT City, AVG(customer_count) as avg_count
  FROM rep_counts
  GROUP BY City
),
kept_reps AS (
  SELECT rc.EmployeeId, rc.City, rc.customer_count
  FROM rep_counts rc
  INNER JOIN city_averages ca ON rc.City = ca.City
  WHERE rc.customer_count > ca.avg_count
),
total_customers AS (
  SELECT SUM(customer_count) as total_count
  FROM rep_counts
)
SELECT 
  kr.City,
  SUM(kr.customer_count) as total_customers,
  AVG(kr.customer_count - ca.avg_count) as avg_excess,
  AVG(kr.customer_count * 1.0 / tc.total_count) as avg_share
FROM kept_reps kr
INNER JOIN city_averages ca ON kr.City = ca.City
CROSS JOIN total_customers tc
GROUP BY kr.City

assumptions.assumption: "the total number of customers matched to any rep across every city" refers to all customers matched to any rep across all cities (the global total), not just customers of kept reps. This makes each rep's share globally comparable.
Cities with no reps strictly above the city average are excluded from results, since there are no reps to return for those cities.
